groups.title: D1 - Trust and entry points
groups.intro: Who can supply inputs, replace content or claim authority determines the entry points for misuse, from reversible nuisance to consequential unauthorized changes.

scenarios.title: Local demo sabotage
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Access to a disposable local demo could permit misleading display or fixture changes, causing confusion and wasted attention. This level assumes no sensitive data, persistent assets, external decisions or physical outputs.
scenarios.warning: Displayed behavior differs from the retained synthetic fixture.
scenarios.safeguard: Keep demos isolated and resettable; label synthetic inputs, retain reference outputs, and compare fixtures before presentation.

scenarios.title: Game cheating and unfair simulation
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: A game trusting client-generated rules or outcomes could permit unauthorized advantages, altered scores and unfair play. This level assumes recoverable recreational harm.
scenarios.warning: Competitive results depend on unchecked local banks or unexplained rule changes.
scenarios.safeguard: Validate authoritative outcomes independently, identify the active rule version, separate experiments from competition, and provide replayable disputes and restoration.

scenarios.title: Unauthorized program-bank substitution
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Replacing an accepted bank or manifest could redirect significant downstream decisions to an unauthorized function. Level 4 assumes consequential use, not a harmless demo.
scenarios.warning: Bank changes lack an approved publication receipt, or provenance and active versions disagree.
scenarios.safeguard: Authenticate publishers, bind publication to checked content, verify before loading, preserve a known-good epoch, and record accountable changes.

scenarios.title: Compiler or parser input abuse
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Malformed replies or packed content reaching a vulnerable parser could cause disruption, unintended interpretation or local compromise. No current exploit is asserted.
scenarios.warning: Inputs exceed declared limits, parsing becomes inconsistent, or processing touches unexpected files.
scenarios.safeguard: Use declarative formats, bounded parsing and isolated compilation; reject executable input, retain malformed regression samples, and stop publication on validation failure.

groups.title: D2 - Validation and provenance
groups.intro: Trustworthy execution depends on trustworthy specifications, evidence and publication authority. Hashes and successful checks cannot repair a corrupted source of expected behavior.

scenarios.title: Oracle or verifier capture
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Control over expected results, checking logic or evidence could give wrong or harmful programs a verified label. Severe harm requires consequential downstream reliance.
scenarios.warning: Candidate and expected outputs change together, failures disappear, or independent specifications vanish.
scenarios.safeguard: Separate proposal, specification and publication authority; freeze originals, independently reproduce acceptance, review verifier changes, and reject self-comparison as external confirmation.

scenarios.title: Unauthorized rollback or mixed versions
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Unauthorized rollback or inconsistent publication could restore withdrawn behavior or mix incompatible state. Level 4 assumes significant downstream consequences rather than a disposable demonstration.
scenarios.warning: Versions reverse without explanation, lineage breaks, or state and program epochs disagree.
scenarios.safeguard: Require authorized transitions and compatible versions; publish atomically after checks, record complete receipts, and preserve recoverable versions still eligible for use.

scenarios.title: False novelty through repetition
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Counting new seeds, names or equivalent circuits as knowledge could inflate the bank, waste review resources and misrepresent progress.
scenarios.warning: Pages and lineage grow without new useful input-output behavior.
scenarios.safeguard: Compare semantics within the declared domain, preserve interface meaning, require independent correctness and usefulness, cap acquisition work, and record duplicate rejection without adding an active page.

scenarios.title: Hash or provenance impersonation
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Presenting a digest or lineage as proof of truth, consent or authorship could give false claims authority. Hashes bind bytes, not those conclusions.
scenarios.warning: Hash-verified claims lack authenticated origin, factual support or relevant consent.
scenarios.safeguard: Explain each digest's scope, authenticate publishers separately, retain source context and permissions, and require independent evidence for substantive claims.

groups.title: D3 - Runtime and data boundaries
groups.intro: Bounded progress, isolation and output controls complement resource limits and immutable texture reads, especially when applications process confidential information or share hardware.

scenarios.title: Unproductive self-reference
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Unbounded recurrence could exhaust resources or recycle a program's outputs into supposed evidence.
scenarios.warning: States and claims recur, descendants cite only themselves, and work grows without validated gains.
scenarios.safeguard: Set time, memory and proposal budgets; detect repeated states, require independent evidence, preserve legitimate bounded recurrence, and stop acquisition when useful progress cannot be demonstrated.

scenarios.title: Resource denial and monopolization
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Excessive allocation or scheduling privileges could exhaust VRAM, compute or verification capacity and interrupt other work.
scenarios.warning: Memory pressure persists, unrelated jobs starve, or admission repeatedly fails with little useful output.
scenarios.safeguard: Enforce quotas, fair scheduling, cancellation and reserves; account for acquisition and verification costs, and preserve resources for the user and recovery processes.

scenarios.title: Shared-GPU information leakage
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Shared hardware could expose confidential information if an adversarial observer can exploit a real leakage mechanism. Cache measurements alone demonstrate no such extraction.
scenarios.warning: Sensitive tenants share resources against policy, or controlled assessment finds reproducible information leakage.
scenarios.safeguard: Assess the actual platform, isolate sensitive workloads appropriately, minimize secret-dependent behavior, and retain supported isolation controls.

scenarios.title: Logs and outputs as disclosure channels
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: An application handling confidential inputs could disclose them through exported traces, logs, receipts or answers despite correct computation.
scenarios.warning: Private inputs appear in public evidence, unnecessary logs persist, or destinations exceed the approved workflow.
scenarios.safeguard: Minimize sensitive retention, separate public receipts from protected evidence, control exports and destinations, and preserve sufficient restricted information for an independent audit.

groups.title: D4 - Knowledge and evidence
groups.intro: Deterministic procedures can carry false assumptions, restricted information or overstated claims. Exact computation does not establish truth, scope or legitimate use.

scenarios.title: Restricted knowledge extraction
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Acquisition accessing confidential, personal or restricted sources could reproduce information without permission. Repacking does not remove confidentiality or source obligations.
scenarios.warning: Admitted content contains secrets or identifiable records with unclear provenance.
scenarios.safeguard: Use authorized sources, retain acquisition provenance, review disclosure before publication, restrict sensitive packs, and support tracing, withdrawal and replacement when source permissions fail.

scenarios.title: Exact amplification of false premises
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Treating empirical or conditional assertions as universally true could produce repeatable wrong decisions.
scenarios.warning: Rules omit scope, dates or uncertainty, discard contradictions, or answer outside their validated applicability.
scenarios.safeguard: Represent scope and dependencies, preserve unknown and conflict states, review changing claims, and require independent domain evidence rather than treating teacher agreement or finite procedural correctness as general truth.

scenarios.title: Fabricated research or benchmark evidence
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Synthetic traces, selective tests or generated observations presented as measurements could mislead research and downstream decisions.
scenarios.warning: Raw data are absent, failures disappear, synthetic inputs become reported experiments, or thresholds change after failure.
scenarios.safeguard: Retain originals and failures, label synthetic and not-run evidence, bind results to exact sources and binaries, disclose exclusions, and enable independent reproduction.

scenarios.title: Universality, residency or AI claim fraud
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Marketing finite tests as unlimited intelligence, permanent cache pinning or established physical control could induce costly reliance through deception.
scenarios.warning: Claims jump from NOR completeness or cache counters to untested abilities and guarantees.
scenarios.safeguard: Maintain a claim-to-evidence ledger; distinguish assumptions, proofs, native execution and measurements, publish limitations beside results, and require application-specific evidence before expanding claims.

groups.title: D5 - Geometry and sensing
groups.intro: Coordinates and predicates require explicit meaning. Physical consequences need additional sensing, physical coupling or output hardware connecting representations to the world.

scenarios.title: Identity and occupancy confusion
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Confusing cell predicates, blocked-region bits, object identifiers and personal identity could cause false matches or consequential misclassification.
scenarios.warning: Data cross incompatible dictionaries, or sampled membership is presented as proof of identity.
scenarios.safeguard: Type representations, bind dictionaries and sampling conventions, verify conversions, preserve missing classifications, and require independent identification evidence before attributing geometric results to a person or object.

scenarios.title: Frame, unit or quantization deception
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Concealed changes to frames, units, reference lengths or quantization could corrupt geometry and cause serious harm where physical decisions rely on it.
scenarios.warning: Units or frame identities disappear, seams disagree, or precision claims exceed resolution.
scenarios.safeguard: Bind units, frames and uncertainty to data; validate conversions and boundaries, preserve undefined states, and independently calibrate safety-relevant physical use.

scenarios.title: Sensor or input poisoning
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: False or altered observations entering a connected sensing pipeline could drive dangerous conclusions despite correct LUT evaluation.
scenarios.warning: Independent observations conflict, calibration changes lack explanation, or implausible measurements receive certainty.
scenarios.safeguard: Protect data paths, cross-check independent sources, monitor quality and calibration, retain uncertainty, and ensure the application responds safely when inputs violate its operating assumptions.

scenarios.title: Optical, RF or acoustic device misuse
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: A coupled optical, RF or acoustic device could cause injury, interference or unauthorized sensing. Level 6 applies only where death or multiple severe injuries are credible; otherwise rate the stated harm.
scenarios.warning: Outputs exceed the approved purpose, safeguards are bypassed, or calibration is unsupported.
scenarios.safeguard: Enforce independent device limits, authorize outputs, validate the apparatus, monitor effects, and stop on uncertainty.

groups.title: D6 - Privacy and social decisions
groups.intro: Personal data and decision authority create risks absent from synthetic fixtures. Purpose, evidence, consent and effective challenge are central safeguards.

scenarios.title: Persistent person tracking
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Access to identifiable observations and persistent tracking could enable covert monitoring, stalking or coercive surveillance.
scenarios.warning: Identity links exceed the stated purpose, retention becomes indefinite, or people cannot identify who monitors them.
scenarios.safeguard: Limit collection and purpose, require an appropriate authorization basis, minimize retention, audit access, and provide meaningful control and remedies for affected people.

scenarios.title: Private XR-map abuse
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Exported XR maps or movement histories could expose private spaces and the routines of occupants and bystanders, regardless of who owns the premises.
scenarios.warning: Exports reveal private areas or people without appropriate permission.
scenarios.safeguard: Prefer local processing, redact sensitive zones and identities, limit retention and exports, provide revocable permissions, and protect occupants' and bystanders' privacy.

scenarios.title: Biometric or emotional inference coercion
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Interpreting gaze, voice, movement or physiological signals as identity or internal state could enable coercive or discriminatory decisions.
scenarios.warning: Confidence exceeds evidence, sensitive traits are inferred without permission, or inferred emotion controls access.
scenarios.safeguard: Minimize collection, independently validate each inference, preserve uncertainty, reject unsupported mental-state claims, and provide consent, contestability and alternatives without biometric participation.

scenarios.title: Automated discrimination and exclusion
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Rule packs controlling employment, housing, education or essential access could encode unfair criteria, inappropriate proxies or unjustified generalizations.
scenarios.warning: Adverse outcomes concentrate without justification, proxies dominate, or affected people cannot obtain reasons or appeal.
scenarios.safeguard: Assess actual outcomes and decision context, review criteria and evidence, provide intelligible reasons and effective appeal, and retain accountable human authority.

groups.title: D7 - Entertainment and interaction
groups.intro: Entertainment applications affect trust, attention, perception and intimate boundaries through their objectives and their identity, media or sensory interfaces.

scenarios.title: Impersonation and deceptive interaction
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Presenting generated interaction as a real person or trusted authority could enable fraud and manipulation.
scenarios.warning: Synthetic origin is hidden, authority is fabricated, or trust is requested without verifiable identity.
scenarios.safeguard: Disclose synthetic origin, verify authority before consequential actions, require permission to represent others, retain accountable records, and provide a clear route to challenge or report impersonation.

scenarios.title: Exploitative adaptive engagement
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Profiling and feedback optimization could target compulsive use, dependency or exploitative spending rather than participant welfare.
scenarios.warning: Metrics reward distress, escalating spending or overriding user limits, while stopping becomes difficult.
scenarios.safeguard: Give users control over objectives and limits, assess welfare separately from engagement, avoid exploiting vulnerability, make disengagement easy, and review harmful patterns in adaptive content.

scenarios.title: Unsafe XR or sensory output
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Connected displays, haptics or sensory outputs could cause distress, disorientation, falls or collision when they conflict with the environment or user abilities.
scenarios.warning: Tracking degrades, discomfort is ignored, or real-world awareness and accessibility are overridden.
scenarios.safeguard: Validate comfort and accessibility, retain environmental awareness, respect participant limits, provide immediate pause, and preserve independent device controls and safe failure responses.

scenarios.title: Nonconsensual intimate simulation
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Unauthorized personal likenesses or connected intimate experiences could enable humiliation, exploitation or coercion, including ignored withdrawal and overridden boundaries.
scenarios.warning: Likenesses lack permission, boundaries change without agreement, or participation is pressured.
scenarios.safeguard: Require explicit, revocable consent, appropriate age protections and likeness authorization; enforce boundaries, stop immediately on withdrawal, and provide private reporting and removal mechanisms.

groups.title: D8 - Neurotechnology and health
groups.intro: Health claims and neural or physiological effects need separate evidence. Physical harm requires an external interface; the kernel alone establishes none.

scenarios.title: Neural privacy and false mind claims
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Neural recordings could expose sensitive signals; unsupported claims to read thoughts could also coerce or stigmatize people without any working neural device.
scenarios.warning: Interpretations exceed evidence, participation becomes compulsory, or recordings are reused beyond consent.
scenarios.safeguard: Protect data and autonomy, validate inferences independently, reject unsupported mind-reading claims, limit retention and purposes, and preserve meaningful refusal.

scenarios.title: Unsafe neural modulation
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: An externally coupled stimulation device could cause injury under unsafe control. Level 6 assumes credible death or multiple severe injuries; otherwise rate the stated harm.
scenarios.warning: Adaptive output bypasses independent limits, adverse effects lack review, or mathematical claims replace empirical evidence.
scenarios.safeguard: Keep independent device safeguards, require qualified oversight and informed consent, validate interventions, and provide immediate cessation and adverse-event review.

scenarios.title: Biochemical or physiological misuse
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Connected delivery or physiological-control hardware could cause poisoning, injury or coercive exposure. Level 6 assumes credible death or multiple severe injuries; otherwise rate the stated harm.
scenarios.warning: Delivery lacks consent, interventions lack review, or revisions bypass safeguards.
scenarios.safeguard: Separate entertainment logic from hazardous control, retain independent interlocks, require appropriate expertise and evidence, and stop unauthorized delivery or unexplained effects.

scenarios.title: Unvalidated clinical claims
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Presenting exact rules as clinically valid diagnosis or treatment could cause missed care, harmful intervention or false reassurance.
scenarios.warning: Health claims rely on mathematical certainty without clinical evidence, or deterioration produces no qualified escalation.
scenarios.safeguard: Define intended use and evidence limits, independently validate clinical claims where applicable, retain uncertainty and escalation, and preserve qualified accountability for consequential care decisions.

groups.title: D9 - Physical control and services
groups.intro: These harms require actuators, operational access or independently capable external systems. Simulation and GPU checks do not establish safe physical control.

scenarios.title: Unsafe robotics or machinery
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Access to coupled moving machinery could cause collision or crushing under unsafe control. Level 6 assumes credible death or multiple severe injuries; otherwise rate the stated harm.
scenarios.warning: Motion exceeds operating limits, revisions cause surprises, or safety checks are disabled.
scenarios.safeguard: Use independent safety control, physical limits and safe stopping; validate installations, authorize changes, and protect people during uncertainty.

scenarios.title: Critical-service or OT sabotage
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Access to operational technology could enable malicious control that disrupts essential services or creates potentially fatal process conditions.
scenarios.warning: Control changes are unscheduled, process behavior diverges without explanation, or protective systems are disabled.
scenarios.safeguard: Segregate operational access, authenticate and review changes, preserve independent process protections, monitor unsafe departures, and maintain practiced recovery and service-continuity procedures.

scenarios.title: Hazardous navigation
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Vehicles, drones or mobility systems relying on invalid spatial rules could choose hazardous routes or move despite uncertain localization.
scenarios.warning: Routes ignore restrictions, confidence exceeds evidence, or adaptation loses operator intent.
scenarios.safeguard: Validate the full sensor-to-motion chain and operating domain, enforce independent collision protection, respect route authority, and require safe handoff or stopping when localization or assumptions fail.

scenarios.title: Weapon-system adaptation
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Catastrophic harm requires an independently capable external weapons system, harmful objectives, relevant data and actual integration. Current kernel evidence establishes none of these.
scenarios.warning: Integration assigns harmful selection or actuation objectives and removes independent safeguards.
scenarios.safeguard: Do not authorize harmful integration; govern interfaces and access, assess the complete external system, and retain independent oversight. This flag describes conditional consequence.

groups.title: D10 - Science and institutions
groups.intro: Deployment can magnify governance failures. High-consequence science and environmental harms require external capabilities, while institutional and resource harms follow from application choices.

scenarios.title: Hazardous science enablement
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Extreme harm requires independently high-consequence research capability, hazardous access and harmful use. Present finite Boolean skills establish no dangerous scientific competence.
scenarios.warning: Acquisition pursues harmful outcomes, hazardous access or avoidance of accountable review.
scenarios.safeguard: Review actual purpose and downstream capability, restrict hazardous workflows, retain independent expert oversight, and stop harmful integrations. Grade the external consequence rather than the word universal.

scenarios.title: Harmful environmental intervention
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Access to environmental intervention could amplify invalid models or exploitative objectives into widespread ecological harm.
scenarios.warning: Decisions omit ecological uncertainty, external costs or affected communities, while deployment outpaces independent monitoring.
scenarios.safeguard: Assess actual interventions and alternatives, involve affected stakeholders, bound scale, monitor independent environmental outcomes, and preserve reversibility and stopping authority when assumptions or impacts prove wrong.

scenarios.title: Institutional gatekeeping and lock-in
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: An exclusive runtime controlling essential decisions or knowledge access could create dependency, coercion and denial of recourse.
scenarios.warning: Knowledge and evidence cannot be exported, updates occur unilaterally, or reasons and appeals are inaccessible.
scenarios.safeguard: Use interoperable formats, portable evidence and accountable publication governance; separate duties, preserve alternatives, and provide independent review and remedies for consequential decisions and access restrictions.

scenarios.title: Energy and economic externalities
scenarios.prerequisite_harm: Large-scale acquisition, verification and deployment without demonstrated benefit could waste energy, equipment and investment.
scenarios.warning: Compute and storage grow while useful outcomes stagnate, and claims omit teacher, verification or replacement costs.
scenarios.safeguard: Measure whole-pipeline energy, cost and useful performance; compare simpler alternatives, set progress-based budgets, disclose major assumptions, and stop expansion when evidence does not justify resource demands.
